title: Simplifying ratios

match.reason: The bank card mat-ratios is broader than the new point, covering unit conversion and sharing quantities as well as simplifying, and it is written at Year 12 depth rather than Year 7.

draft.title: Simplifying ratios
card: A ratio compares quantities in the same units. A ratio of 12 to 18 can be written 12:18.
If the units differ, change them to the same unit first. For 50 cm to 2 m, change 2 m to 200 cm, so the ratio is 50:200.
To simplify, divide each part by their highest common factor (HCF). That is the largest number that divides into both parts exactly.
Example: 12:18. The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6. 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so 12:18 simplifies to 2:3.
draft.remember: Use the same units, then divide both parts by the HCF.

a.why: The HCF of 20 and 30 is 10. 20 ÷ 10 = 2 and 30 ÷ 10 = 3, so the answer is 2:3. The ratio 4:6 is the same ratio, but it can be simplified more by dividing by 2.
a.clue: Find the largest number that divides into both 20 and 30.

b.q: Tane has a rope 1 m long and cuts off a piece 40 cm long. What is the ratio of the piece to the whole rope, in simplest form?
b.why: Change 1 m to 100 cm, so the ratio is 40:100. The HCF is 20, so it simplifies to 2:5. The ratio 40:1 is wrong because it compares different units, cm and m.
b.clue: Change both lengths to centimetres first.
